claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding 2–3 at.% Al and applying homogenization followed by controlled cooling or aging will produce a dual-phase microstructure.
The proposed dual-phase microstructure will contain a disordered BCC matrix.
The proposed dual-phase microstructure will contain finely dispersed B2-ordered precipitates.
The B2-ordered precipitates will be thermally stable under the intended high-temperature conditions.
B2-ordered precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impedance of dislocation motion by B2 precipitates will provide ordering-induced strengthening at high temperature.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The possible yield-strength increase at 1273 K is 20–50% relative to the unmodified alloy.
The modified alloy will retain adequate ductility for service as an intermediate heat-transfer layer.
The modified alloy may have comparable or slightly improved ductility relative to the single-phase alloy.
High-temperature coarsening of the B2 precipitates could reduce the expected performance.
Variations in processing may alter precipitate coarsening and the resulting mechanical properties.
Variations in processing may alter the resulting thermal properties.
The intended application is an intermediate heat-transfer layer between W and CuCrZr operating around 1273 K under structural mechanical loads.
